title: Tie an overhand knot using a jig
instruction: Finish the overhand knot in the blue cord, remove it from the pegs and let go. The knot will be tested with a gentle pull.
context: The jig holds an untied loop for a repeatable cord-finishing step: threading the end, removing the loop and tightening the knot.
setup: One blue round cord, 118 cm between end centres, 8 mm diameter and 46.1 g, approximating braided polyester. The first and last 1 cm links are yellow and red. A fixed grey clamp holds the yellow end. The cord starts with one untied crossing arranged on three rounded 16 mm steel-like pegs, fixed to the standard YAM table. Nothing attaches the cord to the pegs or grippers. The README gives the exact layout and fixture dimensions.
scoring: 0.5: an intact single overhand knot is present at the end of the robot actions, with every robot part at least 3 cm clear of the cord. In a jig trial, the whole cord must also be at least 1 cm clear of every peg and support. 1.0: that knot remains tied and clear throughout a separate pull on the red end away from the permanently clamped yellow end: a 2-second ramp to 0.981 N, then a 5-second hold within ±5%. A failed or unfinished load test retains established 0.5 credit; damaged cord or invalid simulation evidence scores 0. All other outcomes score 0.
run_limit: 2,400 robot control steps (120 seconds at 20 Hz). A separate 7-second evaluator load test follows a qualifying released knot.
reset_notes: Untie the cord and restore the shown single-crossed loop on the three pegs. Keep the yellow end clamped. All parts are reusable.
fidelity: A chain of 118 rigid capsules with bending joints approximates an inextensible round cord. Nonadjacent links collide; grippers use physical contact. An ideal fixed joint represents the standing-end clamp. After robot actions end, the evaluator loads the free end; an equal opposite numerical force is reacted by the fixed end's clamp. This checks external loading, not measured internal tension. Friction and bending are engineering assumptions; braided fibres, stretch and wear are not modelled.
scores: Development draft: no validated robot knot demonstration or Dream run yet.
